features.title: Write a good prompt
features.summary: A prompt is the question or instruction you type. A clear goal is all you need, and extra detail gets you a better answer.
steps: Start with the goal: the task you want done.
Add context: why you need it and who it is for.
Add a source: a file, web page, or your work emails, chats and files.
Add expectations: format, tone or style.
Read the answer, then refine it with follow-up prompts.
prompts: Write a summary based on all emails from Sam in the past two weeks.

Draft an outline of a training manual about time management. Our audience is professionals who work in a hybrid environment and constantly need to attend virtual meetings and meet deadlines. The tone of the document will be friendly and suggestive.

Plan a 3-day trip to Lisbon for two adults. We like food and walking tours, and we want a relaxed pace. Use the flight confirmation I attached to build around our arrival and departure times. Give me a day-by-day itinerary in a table.
limits: Only the goal is required. Add the other parts when you want more specific results.
Responses vary a little each time, so do not expect identical output from the same prompt.
Check answers for accuracy and confirm important details with trusted sources.

source.label: Microsoft Support: Learn about Copilot prompts

features.title: Use work data and name files, people or meetings
features.summary: With the Premium licence, Copilot pulls from your emails, files and meetings automatically. You can also point it at one file, person or meeting.
steps: Sign in with your work account at copilot.cloud.microsoft.
Check that Work IQ is on (the default) so Copilot can use work data.
In your prompt, type a forward slash (/) and then the name of a file, person or meeting.
Pick it from the list, then finish your prompt and send.
To attach something from your device instead, upload a file with your prompt.
prompts: Summarise the key decisions in /[meeting name] and list who owns each action.
What did /[person name] ask me for in emails this week?
Compare /[file name] with last month's version and list what changed.
limits: If you do not reference a source, Copilot picks the best source itself.
With Work IQ off, Copilot answers using only the web and the model's training data.
Basic (no add-on licence) cannot reach work data automatically. You must upload files, use open content in Outlook or Teams, or use a pay-as-you-go agent.
Copilot only sees what you already have permission to see.

source.label: Microsoft Support: Get started with Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat

features.title: Choose Auto, Quick response or Think deeper
features.summary: Copilot can answer fast or slowly with more reasoning. The model picker lets you choose, or leave it on Auto.
steps: Open Copilot Chat.
Find the model picker next to the prompt box. It shows Auto by default.
Leave it on Auto and Copilot chooses for you.
Choose Quick response for routine questions where speed matters.
Choose Think deeper for complex or open-ended questions.
prompts: Give me three bullet points on what this email thread is asking me to do.
Think through the risks of moving our monthly report from Excel to a new tool, and suggest a step-by-step plan.
Draft a one-page proposal for a team away day, with options and trade-offs.
limits: Microsoft says these options update as new models become available, so labels may change.
Anthropic models are only in some licensed experiences and are not available to all users by default.
Quick response is short and succinct. Think deeper takes longer.

source.label: Microsoft Learn: What is Microsoft Copilot? (Model selection)

features.title: Save and share prompts with Prompt Gallery
features.summary: Prompt Gallery holds ready-made prompts from Microsoft and the ones you save. You can share a saved prompt with a team.
steps: Open Prompt Gallery in Copilot Chat, Teams or Outlook.
Browse Suggested for Microsoft-written prompts.
Create and run your own prompt, then hover over it and select the Save prompt icon.
Open the Your prompts tab to find saved prompts.
Hover over a prompt, select Share prompt, then Share to team and choose the team.
prompts: How can I more concisely describe change management?
Summarise this week's updates from my team into five bullet points.
Draft a polite reply declining this meeting and suggesting a new time.
limits: Prompts you save sit under Your prompts. Team prompts sit under Teams.
Each gallery prompt has tips for personalising it.
Prompt Gallery is not yet available in the DoD cloud.
Admins can see saved, liked and shared prompts in analytics.

source.label: Microsoft Support: Sharing prompts with your team

features.title: Find files and people with Copilot Search
features.summary: Search looks across your Microsoft 365 apps for people, files, images, messages and SharePoint sites. You can then move to chat for follow-up.
steps: Open the Microsoft Copilot app.
Select Search in the left navigation.
Type your query and pick a result, or select the Search arrow to see more results.
Use Recent, Shared or Favorites to jump to files.
To narrow results, open the filter menu, select + New, and filter by Location, Shared by or Owned by.
prompts: Q3 budget review slides
Project plan shared by [colleague name]
Meeting notes from last week
limits: The AI-powered Search features need a Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) licence.
Search is available in commercial and government clouds per the service description.
Results only include content you already have access to.

source.label: Microsoft Support: Get started with Search in the Microsoft Copilot app

features.title: Keep your work in Pages and Notebooks
features.summary: A Page turns a Copilot answer into a document you can edit and share. A Notebook gathers files, meetings and emails in one place so Copilot works from them.
steps: For a Page: under a Copilot Chat response, select the ellipses, then Edit in Pages.
Choose an existing Page or a new one, then edit beside Copilot Chat.
For a Notebook: select Notebooks, then All notebooks, then New notebook.
Enter a name. Under Add content to References, add files, meetings, emails or sites.
Select Create, then ask Copilot about your references.
prompts: Summarize the documents in this notebook, highlighting key themes, findings, and next steps.
Summarize the latest updates from my references and draft three discussion points on progress, challenges, and decisions needed.
Draft a one-page proposal from this notebook's files and notes, with an executive summary, objectives, and next steps.
limits: Pages need SharePoint or OneDrive storage, and no Copilot add-on licence is needed for Pages.
Notebooks need a SharePoint or OneDrive service plan. Microsoft's page says some features roll out gradually.
Microsoft's Notebooks page says Copilot Notebooks is now Copilot Workspaces, so names may differ on your screen.
Microsoft gives no file count or size limits on these pages.

source.label: Microsoft Support: Get started with Microsoft 365 Copilot Notebooks

features.title: Use Researcher and Analyst agents
features.summary: Researcher writes a structured, cited report from the web and your work files. Analyst answers questions about data you attach.
steps: Open the Microsoft Copilot app.
Under Agents, select Researcher or Analyst.
Enter a topic or question.
Researcher: answer any clarifying questions, or tell it to proceed, then wait for the report.
Analyst: select the + icon, then Attach content, and choose your data file.
prompts: Create a research summary on sustainable business practices.
Give me a summary of how AI is used in healthcare.
Compare sales data by region and quarter and highlight key trends.
Identify top-performing products or services based on customer engagement metrics.
limits: Researcher needs a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence for business users, and takes longer than normal chat.
Either agent may be unavailable if your administrator has not enabled it.
Researcher is not available in the DoD cloud. Microsoft's pages give no usage quotas.
Researcher replaces Deep Research, which has been retired.

source.label: Microsoft Support: Get started with Researcher in Microsoft 365 Copilot

issues.text: Without the Premium add-on licence (Basic), Copilot Chat cannot read your work data automatically. You must upload files, work from open content in Outlook or Teams, or use a pay-as-you-go agent. Researcher and Analyst can also be missing if your administrator has not enabled them.

source.label: Microsoft Learn: What is Microsoft Copilot?

issues.text: In July 2026 users reported the model picker looking different from Microsoft's docs, with labels like Quick response and Deep response, and some thought manual model choice had gone. One poster said it later returned. No official Microsoft reply in the thread.

source.label: Microsoft Tech Community: Has model selection been removed?

issues.text: File upload limits have been reported as inconsistent. A March 2025 answer said the 1 MB limit was removed (up to 512 MB per prompt), but users in one tenant still saw 1 MB. Check what your own Copilot accepts.

source.label: Microsoft Q&A: File upload limit for Copilot Chat
